assertion_analysis.failure_condition: The bounded wait fails when the predicate stays false until its deadline; replacing cleanup by the base lingering behavior produces that failure.
Fixture positive control fails if any expected non-natural supervisor, harness, child or grandchild is already absent, preventing an empty population from proving cleanup.
Fails if pointer write/read does not preserve the phase supplied by the test; it does not fail when only supervisor pointer observation regresses, as recorded in the finding.
The wait fails if any initially observed process remains alive for 60 seconds; the separate /proc existence assertion fails if reaping leaves even a zombie after supervisor exit.
Fails if the exit receipt is not explicitly attributed to the supervisor.
Fails if adopted-descendant reaping replaces the harness identity with a child PID; restoring the first repair behavior before dd003bc triggers this risk.
Fails when any expected harness or descendant that required intervention is omitted from ended_pids; the crashed harness is correctly excluded because the fixture killed it.
Fails if the supervisor omits forced_exit or records a reason other than terminal-run; removing the new receipt propagation would fail here.
Fails if the intervention receipt omits or misidentifies complete as the terminal phase; this asserts output provenance, whereas line 178 asserts only input setup.
Fails if sender receipts contain no delivered signal outcome, even when a receipt file exists.
Natural-exit positive control fails if supervisor or worker still runs after process.wait returns.
Fails if a natural worker exit is recorded with a nonzero exit code.
Fails if natural exit is recorded as having signalled processes.
Fails if forced_exit is emitted unconditionally instead of only on intervention.
Fails if a natural exit generates any sender log, independently checking the absence of signal activity.
Fails if the supervisor never updates the natural worker pointer from starting to complete; this test does not itself write complete into the pointer.

Fails if the override cap is removed and 3600 seconds is returned; the independent bound is the literal 60 seconds, while the component constants contribute a conservative timing budget rather than proving actual scheduling.

findings.text: non-blocking: this assertion reads complete immediately after the test supplied complete, while STAND_IN also supplies a complete manifest; removing the new pointer deadline at dispatch_launch.py:4811 would leave these assertions and the whole-tree cases satisfiable through manifest cleanup, so add a case with a terminal pointer and a nonterminal or absent manifest to protect pointer-only termination.
